picks.rationale: The most directly actionable item in the pool: working devs lay out how to read an image for provenance, a skill every artist and art director now needs to defend their own work from false accusations.
picks.excerpt: Failbetter, New Blood and other game developers on the importance of honing your visual (and technical) literacy if you want to effectively spot — and fight — genAI art in games.

picks.rationale: A concrete craft blueprint for dynamic NPCs at scale built from systemic design rather than model output — the strongest non-generative answer to the 'AI NPC' pitch this week.
picks.excerpt: ConchShip Games explains how The Scroll of Taiwu drives up to 10,000 dynamic NPCs, 700+ martial arts skills and generational storytelling through systemic sandbox design rather than hand-authored content.

picks.rationale: A per-world procedural magic system is the clearest live demonstration that authored generation still beats generative models at making worlds feel designed — and it ships this year.
picks.excerpt: Dwarf Fortress's long-promised Myth and Magic update will generate a bespoke magic system per world — procedural generation as authored design, not model output.

picks.rationale: A sharp read of what a platform giant actually demoed for AI in games, useful as a reality check on the gap between vendor pitch decks and anything a team could ship.
picks.excerpt: A withering look at Google's AI-in-games sales pitch: '...we are 3-4 years into this collective descent into madness, and this is all you can come up with to support it?'

picks.rationale: Freshest item in the pool and a new front in the AI backlash: the original creator publicly disowning an AI-heavy remake of his own IP, a reputational risk any licensing deal now carries.
picks.excerpt: Original developer Chris Sorrell condemns an AI-heavy James Pond remake as disrespectful and soulless: 'I hope they choke on an AI-generated fishbone.'
